text:
maria: Heads-up — saw a p99 latency spike on several serving hosts (42-47) ~11:02 UTC. Correlates with a sharp eviction_rate jump and sustained memory churn on long-context workloads. Posting short dump and some notes. :eyes:

aj: How big was the p99 delta? any obvious error logs?

maria: p50 stayed ~15ms, p95 ~45ms, p99 jumped from ~90ms to ~360ms for ~6 mins. Eviction_count/sec went 3x. No OOMs, but a lot of pager/reclaim logs: "pager: reclaim started" repeated.

kevin: can you paste the counters and a short scaffold of the log tail?

maria: pasted snippet below:

```
MEM_TOTAL: 62GB  MEM_USED: 58.4GB
KV_CACHE_BYTES: 38.1GB
KV_EVICT_COUNT: 14234 -> 48211  (sustained spike)
KV_REINSERT_COUNT: 1100 -> 7300
KV_PAGING_OPS: 22/s -> 180/s
SERVE_P99: 90ms -> 360ms

[2026-03-17T11:02:01Z] pager: reclaim started (host=42)
[2026-03-17T11:02:03Z] evicter: selected batch=128 cand=4096 (host=42)
[2026-03-17T11:02:03Z] evicter: reinserting key id=0x7f3e... (recent)
[2026-03-17T11:02:04Z] rpc: handler stalled 120ms (waiting for evict lock)
```

kevin: quick read — reinserts up a lot. that suggests churn: entries evicted then immediately reintroduced by concurrent requests for long contexts. under pressure the evicter may be thrashing. i also grep'd for lock order, saw a risky pattern in evicter + pager.

kevin: gist of the problematic section: 

```cpp
// evicter.cpp
std::unique_lock<std::mutex> evict_mu(evict_lock);
// ... calls into pager which takes pager_lock
pager->maybe_page(...); // attempts pager_lock inside
// other code path: rpc handler takes pager_lock then tries evict_lock -> potential inversion
```

kevin: so if a request path holds pager_lock and triggers an evict path that tries to take evict_lock you can get stalls and cascading latency. under high eviction churn that multiplies.

aj: nice catch. lock inversion would explain the ~120ms handler stalls. 2 options: reorder locks to a global canonical order, or make the evicter use try_lock with backoff and offload heavy work to a background thread.

maria: also worth noting that switching the eviction policy from LRU->FIFO on a test cluster reduced p99 briefly, but we saw correctness anomalies during replayed long-context tests: some tokens were recomputed (KV reuse mismatch) — we need to avoid silent correctness changes.

kevin: FIFO probably reduced the reinsert pattern by avoiding promoting entries on read, so fewer churn reinserts. but FIFO exposes other issues when combined with our slab compaction (fragmentation). not a drop-in fix.

sam: propose immediate mitigation: 1) quick patch to avoid lock inversion (hold pager_lock -> never acquire evict_lock; enforce canonical order) 2) add a short evicter_hysteresis window to avoid re-evicting recently inserted entries for 200ms. 3) run kvbench replay to validate correctness. i can run this in staging.

aj: +1. also instrument a hotset_age histogram so we can see age distribution of evicted entries. that'll tell us whether we are evicting very-fresh items.

maria: sam — push the staging run. i opened a lightweight tracing span around the evict path (evict.span) to get stack context.

sam: command i'll run in staging: `./kvbench --workers 64 --context-len 65536 --pattern long-context --duration 10m --collect evict,reinserts,locks`

dev-bot: deploy evicter/lock-order-fix -> staging succeeded (build: evicter-2026-1032) :white_check_mark:

sam: early staging numbers (10m after deploy): p99 back to ~72ms, eviction_rate down ~3x, reinserts down ~80%. hotset_age shows a small mode at <50ms previously, now shifted to 450ms+.

maria: excellent. that strongly points to dangerous thrash + lock inversion amplification. can we keep hysteresis disabled in prod until we confirm no correctness regressions? i want a slow canary.

aj: let's ship lock-order fix to 10% canary in prod, monitor evict_count, reinserts, p99, and hotset_age. if stable for 30m, roll to 50% then 100%.

kevin: long term ideas: (a) make evicter cooperative (batch eviction with async delete), (b) per-shard aging metrics + adaptive thresholds, and (c) small read-only promotion instead of full reinserts to avoid extra allocation churn.

maria: agreed. i'll file an RFC for cooperative eviction + promotion semantics. for now, rolling the lock-order fix + controlled canary. @sam please also add a perf-regression test that replays the long-context traces we saw. :thumbsup:

sam: will do. linking dashboard for the canary: https://perf.redwood.internal/dashboards/evicter/1768889999 (monitoring pinned) — will update every 10m.

maria: thanks all, keeping this thread pinned. follow-ups: rfc + test + small ops runbook for hysteresis.

aj: thanks, great triage.

kevin: nice triage team.

sam: 30m check-in: still stable, leaving canary at 10% for 1h then bumping if green.

maria: copy — good work. :white_check_mark:
